headline: US stocks closed higher for the week as tech rebounded and Trump-Putin diesel deal eased fuel concerns despite 10-year yields climbing above 5%
raw_text:
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) rose 423 points, or 0.83%, to 51,654.95, the S&P 500 ($SPX) gained 0.59% to 7,811.54 near its record high, and the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) added 0.64% to 27,366.17 for a fourth straight weekly advance as technology shares rebounded and AI concerns eased.
- President Trump’s agreement with Vladimir Putin paused some sanctions and secured the immediate release of 2.2 million barrels of Russian diesel fuel to ease price pressures tied to Hurricane Isaias.
- Real estate led sector gains with a 1.9% advance as Crown Castle (CCI) climbed 15.6% and American Tower (AMT) rose 9.3%.
- Humana (HUM) jumped 11.6% after improving its Medicare Advantage star ratings, which should boost future revenue, and receiving an analyst upgrade.
- Biotech names rallied, with Moderna (MRNA) up 14.1% and Novavax (NVAX) up 15.9%.
- Delta Air Lines (DAL) traded roughly flat after reporting Q3 EPS of $1.72 versus $1.76 expected and cutting full-year guidance, citing roughly $500 million in extra fuel costs from higher oil (@CL) prices linked to Hurricane Isaias and Middle East tensions.
- Communication services lagged with a 1.4% decline as telecom stocks fell, including AT&T (T) down 9.8%, T-Mobile US (TMUS) off 13.3%, and Verizon (VZ) lower by about 10% on fears that SpaceX (SPCX)’s acquisition of nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum will intensify wireless competition.
- Nine of 11 S&P 500 ($SPX) sectors advanced on the day.
- The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.24% as the national debt exceeded $40.3 trillion and consumer sentiment slipped to its lowest level since May.
- After-hours trading was muted with no major earnings moves above 2%, and investors are looking ahead to big bank earnings next week from firms including JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Goldman Sachs (GS).
